# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for detailed Q&A)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "Ruth Fielding at Golden Pass; or, The Perils of an Artificial Avalanche" by Alice B. Emerson (Cupples & Leon, 1925; Gutenberg #76206)

### Cast
- **Ruth Fielding**: heroine; orphan raised by great-uncle Jabez Potter & Aunt Alvirah Boggs at the Red Mill near Cheslow; scenario writer/director of Fielding Film Corporation; "my pretty" (Aunt Alvirah's term).
- **Tom Cameron**: Helen's twin; Ruth's business partner; loves Ruth; jealous of Layton Boardman; "Tommy-boy"; rifle-hunter; heroic rescuer.
- **Helen Cameron**: Ruth's chum; engaged to Chess Copley; flippant, lively.
- **Chess (Charles) Copley**: Helen's fiancé; his uncle backs his business deal.
- **Jennie Marchand** ("Heavy", née Stone): married to Henri Marchand, a Frenchman in France.
- **Ann Hicks**, **Nettie Parsons**, **Mary Cox** ("The Fox"), **Mercy Curtis** (lives in Cheslow): school chums from Briarwood Hall. Mary Cox's escort: Charles.
- **Barclay Clayton ("Bark")**: escort at theater.
- **Mr. Hammond**: president of Alectrion Film Corporation; suggests Ruth act; arranges Edith Lang.
- **Layton Boardman**: western actor, hired as hero (ex-Palatial Films, feud with Sol Bloomberg); dark hair, gray eyes; injured in fall from horse; flirts with Ruth; later says he "never cared for girls" (acting).
- **Viola Callahan**: temperamental actress, lead of "Hearts of the Mountains"; jumps contract (note: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg..."); lover Tony Martano.
- **Charlie Reid**: Sol Bloomberg's agent; met Viola in Chicago.
- **Sol Bloomberg**: owner of Palatial Films; enemy.
- **Edith Lang**: crippled ex-actress (WWI Red Cross, lost leg), coaches Ruth.
- **Ma and Pa Gowdy**: owners of Headwaters Ranch near Golden Pass, Montana. **Andy**: gangling lad. Foreman: long, lean, blue-eyed.
- **Shepley**: tall thin director, Ruth's right hand. **Dave Sentner**: comedian.
- **Mr. Farstein**: Cheslow theater manager.
- **Uncle Jabez Potter** (crabbed), **Aunt Alvirah Boggs** (little old woman).
- Film titles: "Snowblind" (first hit), "The Heart of a Schoolgirl," "Hearts of the Mountains."

### Sequence of events
1. Opening night of "Snowblind" in Cheslow (Palace theater). Chums (led by Heavy/Jennie, Ann, Helen-"S.B." yell) surprise Ruth at Red Mill. Ruth speaks on stage; explosion of film storeroom; smoke, lights out.
2. Tom rescues Ruth behind stage; Uncle Jabez and Aunt Alvirah; party at Cheslow hotel. Mr. Hammond appears, mentions Golden Pass, Montana (cattle round-up; he stopped there).
3. Ruth decides to film in Golden Pass. Hires Boardman (contract; Tom reluctant; "I don't like that fellow").
4. Helen's news: Chess's uncle funds business deal; she and Chess will marry. Tom jokes.
5. Viola hired at high salary; Tom quarrels over salary.
6. House party at Red Mill; Boardman dances; Tom jealous ("watch my step").
7. Train to Chicago; Viola seen talking to Charlie Reid (Bloomberg's agent); suspicion.
8. Train to Montana; Headwaters Ranch.
9. Stampede of steers; Boardman tries to save Ruth, thrown from horse, ankle/back injured; Tom shoots steers, saves Ruth.
10. Helen hurt by spent bullet at rodeo (real cartridge); Ruth tends her with Red Cross training.
11. Viola jumps contract (note); Mr. Hammond arrives, proposes Ruth act lead.
12. Ruth tests on camera; Tom jealous; Edith Lang arrives to coach.
13. Tom meets bear at water hole; Ruth finds him.
14. Narrow ledge: Ruth falls; Tom rescues her, uses lariat via Boardman; Tom's arm injured later.
15. Avalanche (planted dynamite) — second explosion from dynamite house buries cave; Tom finds tunnel; two bears in cave; Tom shot them, arm mauled; Ruth's twig tourniquet saves him.
16. Chess arrives; Boardman tells Tom he "never cared for any girl."
17. Ruth's picture "Hearts of the Mountains" premieres in New York; Viola/Bloomberg's picture fails. Ruth: "So are the wicked punished!"

### Other details
- Ruth's picture advertised in electric lights; Ruth lifted to stage by audience.
- Tom's arm and Ruth's tourniquet (twig) — doctor "old doctor... thick-rimmed glasses."
- Ma Gowdy: tall, calico dress. Ranch flivver: rickety car.
- Mr. Hammond lingers past intention.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Clock Struck One" by Fergus Hume (Frederick Warne, 1898; Gutenberg #55689)

### Cast
- **Dora Carew**: heroine, tall, gold-haired, gray-eyed, bicycling "Diana of Kent"; ward of Julian Edermont; affianced to Allen.
- **Dr. Allen Scott**: young doctor in Canterbury; son of Dr. Scott (shot 20+ yrs ago); housekeeper Mrs. Tice (his old nurse).
- **Julian Edermont** (real name **Julian Dargill**): recluse at the Red House, Chillum, near Canterbury; small, white-haired, bearded, timid; prayer "From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us." Murdered.
- **Lambert Joad**: old parasite, ex-clergyman, alcoholic, lusts after Dora; sleeps in cottage across road from 9 pm to 9 am; hides manuscript; altered hall clock; died of heart disease.
- **Lady Laura Burville** (born Laura Treherne; "L.B." pearl brooch): Dora's mother; married Carew, then Dargill, then Sir John Burville (African millionaire, violent). Guest at Hernwood Hall.
- **Augustus Pallant**: red-haired blackmailer; blackmailed Laura; later shot in San Francisco gambling shop.
- **John Mallison / Mr. Pride**: schoolmaster at Chillum, chubby, silver hair; killer of Edermont; executed.
- **George Theophilus Carew** (Captain, Dora's supposed father): shot Dr. Scott by mistake; died in San Francisco (in Pallant's arms).
- **Dr. Scott senior** (Allen's father), killed by mistake.
- **Mr. Carver**: lawyer, Canterbury, office near Mercery Lane.
- **Inspector Jedd**: Canterbury police; "tramp" theory.
- **Dr. Chambers**: Canterbury doctor, time of death.
- **Meg Gance**: cook/servant at Red House; hall clock wrong.
- **Sir Harry Hernwood**: Hernwood Hall host; gave Laura's address (22 Jersey Place, Mayfair).
- **Emma**: servant at Scott's house.

### Sequence of events
1. Dora bicycles to meet Allen, July noon, bridge two miles from Canterbury. Lady Burville (guest at Hernwood Hall) fainted in Chillum Church; Edermont fainted at her sight during Litany.
2. At Red House: Joad admits them; Edermont shrieks from window; Allen flees.
3. Edermont tells Allen secret (quarrel); bars Allen from Dora; warns Dora against Lady Burville.
4. Dora visits Mrs. Tice in Canterbury; Mrs. Tice shows photo of young Edermont; lies about parents.
5. Mr. Pallant brings Edermont "good news" (enemy Carew dead); Edermont faints with joy.
6. Edermont writes to Allen; Dora at study on Aug 2; hears "one" from hall clock.
7. Murder discovered morning Aug 3: Edermont's head beaten with Zulu knobkerrie, bureau smashed, pistol nearby. Meg finds body; Joad arrives early.
8. Allen tells Dora he will end engagement; she refuses to release him.
9. Inquest: five witnesses (Meg, Dora, Joad, Dr. Chambers, Jedd). Verdict: murder by person unknown.
10. Will: Dora gets Red House + £200/yr (conditions: stay there, Joad remains); £50,000 to whoever punishes assassin; Dora supposedly £500/yr income — Carver says false.
11. Dora sees Allen at home; Mrs. Tice's cover; Dora asks Mrs. Tice to stay at Red House.
12. Joad courts Dora; threatens: accuses Allen of murder (seen at ~midnight). Gives a week.
13. Dora confronts Allen in dining room; Allen: "I was mad on that night"; letter from Edermont; brooch (L.B.) found in study.
14. Dora visits Sir Harry; gets Laura's address; meets Laura in London; Laura reveals she is Dora's mother.
15. Laura's story: married Carew; widowed; married Dargill (Edermont); daughter Dora; Carew alive; Dargill fled; Laura married Burville. Pallant blackmailed.
16. Mrs. Tice's story: Dr. Scott shot by Carew; Allen's father killed.
17. Dora deduces Joad put clock an hour fast (Meg: clock an hour wrong). Dora searches Joad's cottage; finds manuscript ("Confession of Julian Dargill").
18. Joad confesses to Carver; Carver reveals: Pride = John Mallison, killer. Edermont had written to Mallison cutting pension. Mallison killed Edermont; Joad, a witness, was forced into silence.
19. Allen and Dora learn Dora is Dargill's daughter; no bar to marriage; Dora inherits £50,000 via Joad's will.
20. Final: Joad dies of heart attack on arrest night. Pallant shot in San Francisco. Mallison confesses, executed. Laura re-married by Sir John. Dora & Allen to marry in spring; move to Harley Street (Allen's plan) or Canterbury.

### Other details
- Hall clock: Joad put it an hour fast; hall clock chimed one; actual murder at ~12.
- Brooch: slender pale gold bar, two pearl letters "L.B."
- Dora's bicycle; Allen's bicycle.
- Carver: "Mr. Carver the misogamist."
- Pallant's line: "Beware of Allen Scott!"
- Mallison's confession: "I did kill Julian Dargill."
